sections.h2: How is South Dakota organized when you sell a house?
sections.html:
South Dakota has 66 counties, and almost every step of a home sale runs through one of them. The population range is wide: Jones County has 913 residents and Minnehaha County, home to Sioux Falls, has 212,691.

Two counties, Todd and Oglala Lakota, have no county seat of their own. Winner in Tripp County and Hot Springs in Fall River County serve as their administrative centers. Six counties sit entirely inside an Indian reservation, so a seller there should confirm which offices and rules apply to a particular parcel.

The city you live in matters less than the county the parcel sits in. Our county guides cover Minnehaha, Pennington and Lincoln counties, and our city pages cover Sioux Falls, Rapid City, Aberdeen and Brookings.

sections.h2: Which county office do I call about a house?
sections.html:
Call the office that matches the question. The Department of Revenue splits it in two: ask the county Director of Equalization about the assessed value, and ask the county Treasurer about the tax bill.

  • Director of Equalization: acts as the assessor for all real property in the county.
  • Auditor: figures the tax levies for the taxing entities in the county.
  • Treasurer: collects property taxes for the county, cities and school districts.
  • Register of Deeds: keeps land title transfers and other local records.

The state does not collect or spend property tax money, according to the Department of Revenue. Property is assessed at full and true value and then equalized to 85 percent. A home with a full and true value of $230,000 has a taxable value of $195,500 in the department's own example. Our South Dakota property tax guide walks through appeals and relief programs.

sections.h2: When are South Dakota property taxes delinquent?
sections.html:
Half of the unpaid real property tax becomes delinquent on May 1, and the other half on November 1 if it is not paid by October 31. State law adds interest on the first day of each month after a delinquency date, at the rate tied to SDCL 54-3-16.

ItemRuleSource
First half delinquentMay 1SDCL 10-21-23
Second half delinquentNovember 1SDCL 10-21-23
Bills of $50 or lessPaid in full by April 30SDCL 10-21-23
State transfer fee$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction, paid by the sellerSDCL 43-4-21
Foreclosure redemptionOne year from the sale date in most casesSDCL 21-52-11
Security deposit refund21 days after the tenancy endsSDCL 43-32-24
Time limit to open probateThree years after death, with exceptionsSDCL 29A-3-108

A payment postmarked by the last day before delinquency counts, and a deadline that falls on a weekend moves to the last working day of the month. Ask the county Treasurer for an exact payoff before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What does the seller pay at transfer in South Dakota?
sections.html:
The seller pays a state transfer fee of fifty cents for each five hundred dollars of value, or fraction of that, under SDCL 43-4-21. On a $250,000 sale that works out to $250.

The statute lists many transfers the fee does not reach. A few that come up with houses:

  • Sheriff's deeds and other deeds issued in foreclosure actions, or in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Transfers under a decree of distribution in a decedent's estate.
  • Transfers between a fiduciary and a beneficiary to accommodate the fiduciary relationship.
  • Gifts with no consideration, and transfers pursuant to a divorce decree.

An ordinary sale for money is not on that list, so plan for the fee unless your title company tells you otherwise. The county Register of Deeds is where the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: How does foreclosure work in South Dakota?
sections.html:
South Dakota allows two routes. A mortgage that contains a power of sale can be foreclosed by advertisement, which happens outside court. Otherwise the lender files a foreclosure action in the circuit court of the county where the property sits.

Foreclosure by advertisement follows a fixed script under SDCL chapter 21-48:

  • The lender publishes notice once a week for four successive weeks in a legal newspaper of the county.
  • At least 21 days before the sale, the lender serves written notice on the owner and on lienholders.
  • The sheriff sells the property at public auction in the county.
  • Any surplus after the debt is paid goes to the clerk of the circuit court, and the sheriff mails notice of the deposit to the owner and junior lienholders.

An owner can ask a court to require foreclosure by action instead, under SDCL 21-48-9. After the sale, most people entitled to redeem have one year from the sale date, with a shorter 180 day period for a redemption mortgage. Paying certain amounts before the year ends can extend redemption by another year. Because the sale does not end the owner's rights right away, a seller facing a notice should speak with a South Dakota attorney about timing. A cash sale before the auction date can close the matter while you still hold title.

sections.h2: Does a South Dakota house have to go through probate before it can be sold?
sections.html:
Not always. South Dakota lets successors claim real property by affidavit sixty days after death when the decedent's interest in all South Dakota real property is $50,000 or less. The affidavit and a death certificate are filed with the register of deeds in every county where the decedent owned land.

The same statute protects the buyer: a purchaser acting in good faith, for value, takes title free of estate claims and has no duty to ask whether the transfer was proper. A mortgage or judgment lien still stays on the property.

When the interest is larger, a personal representative handles it. SDCL 29A-3-715 lets a personal representative sell real property of the estate for cash or on credit, unless the will or a court order says otherwise. If the market value is not readily ascertainable, written notice of the sale goes out at least fourteen days before closing to anyone who filed a demand for notice. Proceedings generally cannot begin more than three years after the death. Our probate guide for South Dakota covers creditor deadlines and closing the estate.

sections.h2: How does the homestead rule affect a sale?
sections.html:
The homestead protection in SDCL chapter 43-31 shields the family home from judicial sale and judgment liens, and it still applies while the home is listed for sale. It covers one dwelling and its appurtenant buildings, up to one acre inside a town plat or 160 acres outside one.

Two points matter at closing. A married owner's conveyance of a homestead is valid when both spouses sign, so a deed with one signature can stall a closing. And the homestead stays liable for taxes that accrue on it. A separate tax rule exempts a homestead worth less than $170,000, owned by someone 70 or older or by that person's unremarried surviving spouse, from sale for taxes while it remains a homestead.

Ask the title company which signatures it needs before you accept any date.

sections.h2: What if the house has tenants?
sections.html:
A sale does not erase a lease, so the rental rules stay in force until the tenancy ends. Our South Dakota landlord and tenant guide covers entry notice, eviction steps and repairs in more detail.

  • A security deposit cannot exceed one month's rent, unless special conditions pose a danger to maintenance of the premises.
  • The landlord must return the deposit or give a written reason for withholding within 21 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant's mailing address is received.
  • Bad faith retention can bring punitive damages of up to $200.
  • An eviction action is allowed when a tenant holds over after the term or fails to pay rent for three days after it is due (SDCL 21-16-1).

Pull the deposit records and the lease before you accept an offer, since the buyer will ask for both.

sections.h2: What does an as-is cash sale mean here?
sections.html:
It means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and you skip repairs, staging and showings. The county and state steps above still apply: taxes are settled at closing, the transfer fee is due unless an exemption applies, and the deed is recorded with the Register of Deeds.

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal, so the sale can close on a schedule you choose. That can help when a May 1 or November 1 tax date is near, when an auction date has been set, or when heirs live out of state. Ask the title company to confirm every payoff before you sign, and ask the county office whenever a rule here depends on your parcel.

faqs.q: How many counties does South Dakota have?
faqs.a: South Dakota has 66 counties. Property tax, recording and foreclosure sales are all handled at the county level.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the county Treasurer for the bill and the Director of Equalization for the assessed value.

faqs.q: When do South Dakota property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: One half becomes delinquent May 1 and the other half November 1, and interest then accrues monthly.

faqs.q: Who pays the South Dakota transfer fee?
faqs.a: The seller pays fifty cents per five hundred dollars of value or fraction, unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Can I sell during a foreclosure?
faqs.a: Yes. Most people entitled to redeem have one year from the sale date, and a sale before the auction can pay off the loan. Talk with a South Dakota attorney first.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If the decedent's South Dakota real property is worth $50,000 or less, successors can file an affidavit after sixty days.

faqs.q: Do both spouses have to sign the deed?
faqs.a: For a married owner's homestead, the conveyance is valid when both spouses sign.

faqs.q: What if I rent the house to tenants?
faqs.a: The lease stays in effect. The deposit must be returned or accounted for within 21 days after the tenancy ends.
